explanation: L5/H5 turns an open-class anchor into a predicate-verb prior: it attends almost one-hot (weight 1.0 in 18 of 20 top examples, at the current token or the last content word before it) and writes that token's layer-5 value, whose logit lens is exactly the set of verbs that can follow it (indicate, show, reveal, suggest, demonstrate, have), and mean-ablating the head costs those verbs plus the copulas that follow a subject ('are', 'were', 'is', 'suggest', 'show', 'indicate', 'have'; KL 0.05, spread over many verb forms, which is why the protocol's concentration test reads the mechanism as retrospective rather than lookahead). Strength is how far that write sits from the head's mean write: 2.6-3.6 for abstract, usually plural deverbal nominals (findings, observations, results, pressures, experiments, estimates, studies, warnings, comments, differences), 1.2-2.3 for concrete count nouns and finite verbs (cats, bottles, tables, slept, failed), near the median (0.0-0.3) for function words in running prose and for the sequence's first token, which it attends when nothing else matches, and a strong anchor's value is re-written at later nominals of its phrase ('The results of the study of the trial' reads 2.9 at all three nouns), so a text is inactive when it offers no open-class anchor at all - a single token, one frequent token repeated, or a digit/number run (0.0-0.5, at any length) - while short generic clauses are borderline ('The chair was clear.' 0.9, 'The dog was clear.' 1.2) and closed-class strings, symbol runs, non-Latin script and code cross at whichever fragment token spikes.
